info.name: DOST Meeting Management
info.description: Auth, Meeting CRUD, and Participant management endpoints for the DOST meeting management API. Run **Login** first to populate the `token` collection variable; subsequent requests use it via Bearer auth.

request.description: Creates a new user. Returns `{ token, user }` and sets the `token` collection variable on success.
Returns `{ token, user }`. Test script auto-saves `token` to the collection variable.
Returns the user attached to the current bearer token.
Returns `{ users: [...] }` (id, name, email, role, department, createdAt) for the user directory. Any signed-in user can call it.

Admin only (403 for staff). Partial update: `name`, `email`, `role`, `department`, `password`. `role` must be `staff` or `admin` (400 otherwise); `id` must be a UUID; `email` must be valid; a non-empty `password` needs at least 8 characters (empty leaves it unchanged). An admin cannot edit their own account (400). Returns `200 { user }` or 404.
Admin only (403 for staff). An admin cannot delete their own account (400). Returns 204.

Creates a meeting with an immutable registered-user `ownerId` and sends the organizer a best-effort `METHOD:REQUEST` calendar email with `SEQUENCE:0`. `ownerId` defaults to the caller for backwards compatibility; the owner and creator are both organizers when they differ. `startsAt`/`endsAt` accept ISO 8601 with offset; Postgres normalizes to UTC. `timezoneName` defaults to `'UTC'` if omitted; must be a valid IANA zone.

Returns `{ meetings: [...] }` for the meetings the caller owns or attends. Admins receive every meeting by default; add `scope=mine` to limit an admin to their own (`scope=all` is the default and does nothing for staff). Also returns pagination headers:
- `X-Total-Count`: total matching rows
- `Link` (RFC 5988): `first`, `last` always; `prev`/`next` at boundaries; preserves filter query params.

Each meeting includes `tagId`, `tag`, `fileCount`, `fileNames`, `participantCount`, and `participantNames`; `fileNames` lists uploaded filenames for repository search/display, `participantCount` is the full attendee count, and `participantNames` is a short preview of up to three names for repository/list views.

query.description: plainto_tsquery over title + description (english config, stemmed) and uploaded file names (simple config); max 200 chars

request.description: Returns `{ meeting }` to the meeting owner, a participant, or an admin (403 otherwise). Meeting responses include `tagId`, `tag`, `calendarSequence`, `fileCount`, `fileNames`, `participantCount`, and `participantNames`; `calendarSequence` is the persistent ICS revision, `fileNames` lists uploaded filenames, and `participantNames` is a short preview of up to three names.

Partial update for the meeting owner, an organizer, or an admin. Changes to title, description, start/end, timezone, or location increment `calendarSequence` and send a best-effort `METHOD:REQUEST` ICS to participants and emailed external invitees. Cancellation increments the sequence and sends `METHOD:CANCEL`; same-value, tag-only, completion, and archival updates do not send calendar email.
Hard delete for the meeting owner, an organizer, or an admin. Returns 204 on success, 403 for other callers, or 404 if not found.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Quarterly Operations Review",
  "tag": "Operations",
  "ownerId": "<owner-user-uuid>",
  "description": "Review delivery health and risks",
  "durationMinutes": 60,
  "timezoneName": "Australia/Brisbane",
  "responseDeadline": "2026-05-08T17:00:00+10:00"
}

request.description: Creates a meeting request with an immutable registered-user `ownerId`. A distinct owner is retained in the invitation list and becomes an organizer when confirmed. `ownerId` defaults to the caller for backwards compatibility. `responseDeadline` is required, must be a future ISO 8601 datetime, controls when invitee availability submission closes, and must remain strictly earlier than every candidate time option.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Quarterly Operations Review",
  "tag": "Operations",
  "description": "Review delivery health and updated risks",
  "durationMinutes": 90,
  "timezoneName": "Asia/Manila",
  "responseDeadline": "2026-05-08T17:00:00+08:00"
}

request.description: Updates editable meeting request details before the request is closed. Used when the organizer goes back in the creation wizard and changes duration, timezone, title, tag, description, or response deadline. The response deadline must remain strictly earlier than every existing candidate time option; invalid updates return 400.

Replaces candidate time options. Every option must start strictly after the response deadline; earlier or equal starts return 400. Returns 409 if any option overlaps the request creator's existing non-cancelled/non-archived meetings.

Generates expiring per-invitee tokens and sends availability links through the configured email provider (SMTP or Resend). Returns `{ sentCount }`. Copy a token from the test mailbox into the `invitationToken` collection variable to exercise the public endpoints.
Returns invitee-safe request detail for a valid, unexpired email token without requiring a user account.
Submits availability using the email token. Returns 404 for invalid or expired tokens and 409 after the response deadline or request closure.

Invitee-safe request detail for the dashboard voting modal. Returns `{ meetingRequest, invitee, timeOptions, responses }` for the matching invitee or request creator. `meetingRequest` includes derived `responseDeadlinePassed`, `availabilityClosed`, and `canConfirm` flags.
Submit or replace an invitee's binary availability responses. Returns `409` after the request response deadline has passed.

Allows the request creator to choose an existing time option and create the scheduled meeting before or after all invitees respond. Confirming closes outstanding availability voting and sends best-effort confirmation emails containing the Markdown agenda and a sequence-zero `METHOD:REQUEST` ICS to the organizer and previously emailed invitees. Returns `{ meeting, meetingRequest, emailDelivery: { sentCount, failedCount } }`.

item.name: Dashboard
item.description: Dashboard aggregate data for the signed-in user, including host-created pending meeting requests and invitee availability requests before they become confirmed meetings.

request.description: Returns `{ recentMeetings, pendingMeetingRequests, pendingAvailabilityRequests, myActionItems }`. `recentMeetings` includes the next six accessible active meetings ordered by earliest start time. `pendingMeetingRequests` includes unconfirmed, uncancelled meeting requests created by the current user, including derived deadline flags. `pendingAvailabilityRequests` includes requests where the current user is an invitee, still needs to submit availability, and the response deadline has not passed. `myActionItems` includes lean summaries for the current user's open assigned action items, including derived `isOverdue` and `dueState`; fetch `/action-items/:id` for detail-only fields.

Topbar-friendly notification payload. Returns `{ unreadCount, notifications, nextCursor }`, where `notifications` contains the latest five notification previews and `nextCursor` is present when more items exist.

query.description: Optional page size, defaults to 20 and caps at 50
Optional cursor returned by the previous page

request.description: Cursor-paginated notification feed. Returns `{ notifications, nextCursor }`; pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` to fetch the next page.
Marks one notification owned by the signed-in user as read. Returns `{ notification }`.
Archives one notification owned by the signed-in user. Archived notifications are marked read and hidden from summary/feed responses. Returns `{ notification }`.
Marks selected notifications owned by the signed-in user as read. Returns `{ updatedCount }`.
Marks every unread notification owned by the signed-in user as read. Returns `{ updatedCount }`.
Archives all read notifications owned by the signed-in user. Unread notifications are preserved. Returns `{ archivedCount }`.

item.name: Minutes
item.description: Manage minutes for a meeting. `content`, `keyDiscussions`, `decisions`, `facilitatorId`, `recorderId`, and optional `generatedFromTranscriptId` live on `/meetings/{{meetingId}}/minutes`, not on the meeting record.

request.description: Returns `{ minutes }` to the meeting owner, a participant, or an admin. If the meeting has no minutes yet, the API creates an empty draft minutes row.

body.raw:
{
  "content": "Reviewed delivery risk and agreed follow-up owners.",
  "keyDiscussions": "Timeline risk\nResourcing",
  "decisions": "Keep current milestone scope.",
  "facilitatorId": null,
  "recorderId": null,
  "generatedFromTranscriptId": null
}

request.description: Updates moved minutes fields. Only the meeting owner, an organizer, or an admin can update minutes.
Updates the meeting's current minutes row, creating a draft row first if needed.
Expected 400 with `No updates supplied`.
Expected 404.
Expected 404 with `Minutes not found`.

Applies a reviewed analysis run to the draft minutes. Owner, organizer, or admin only.

`expectedVersion` is required. Send the version the client currently holds; the guard is in the UPDATE's WHERE clause, so a human edit landing in between cannot be overwritten.

409 returns `{ error, currentVersion, minutes }` and changes nothing. Do not retry automatically — show the user what changed first.

Writes content, key_discussions, decisions, and generated_from_transcript_id. The result stays `draft`: applying never approves or publishes, and the analysis provider is not called again.

item.name: Recordings
item.description: Manage the single active meeting recording used for transcript/minutes generation. This is separate from regular Meeting Materials files, which can also include audio. When `AI_PIPELINE_ENABLED=true`, upload returns an `uploaded` recording, a `processing` transcript, and a `queued` analysis run while the separate server worker publishes Redis Stream jobs from the PostgreSQL outbox.

request.description: Returns `{ recording, transcript, analysisRun }`. All are null when no active recording exists. Any meeting participant (or an admin) can read recording metadata, transcript status, and analysis-run status.

formdata.description: Select an MP3/WAV/M4A audio file ≤ 50 MB
Required. Must be true: confirms every participant agreed to the recording (otherwise 400)
Set true to replace the current active recording

request.description: Owner, organizer, or admin only. Uploads the one active recording used for minutes generation. Returns `{ recording, transcript: null, analysisRun: null }`; generation does not start until the Generate minutes request. Without `replace=true`, a second active recording returns 409. Every upload must send `consentConfirmed=true`, otherwise it returns 400.

Owner, organizer, or admin only. Queues Speech-to-Text and analysis for the active recording. Returns 202 with `generationStatus='queued'`, the processing transcript, and the queued analysis run. A request while generation is already active returns 409.
Owner, organizer, or admin only. Archives the active recording and removes its MinIO object. Returns 204.

Server-sent events for one meeting's recording workflow. Available to the owner, participants, and admins; anyone else gets a normal 403 before the stream opens.

Frames: `snapshot` (PostgreSQL state, always first on every connection), `status` (a transition, reloaded from PostgreSQL rather than forwarded from Redis), `settled` (transcription reached completed or failed; the server then closes), `error` (stream ended early, e.g. access revoked mid-stream), and `: heartbeat` comment frames every WORKFLOW_SSE_HEARTBEAT_MS.

Payloads carry identifiers, statuses, error messages, timestamps, and segmentCount only. Never transcript text, audio, credentials, or presigned URLs — refetch GET /meetings/{{meetingId}}/recording after `settled` for the transcript body.

Meeting access is authorised before any stream header is written, so a non-participant receives 403 rather than an empty 200.

Authenticate with the Authorization header. EventSource cannot send one, so browser clients use fetch. Never put the JWT in a query parameter.

Postman shows the raw stream; it will not close on its own until `settled` arrives.

The latest analysis for the meeting, for any participant or an admin.

Returns `{ analysisRun, suggestions, transcript }`. The run carries summary, keyDiscussions, decisions, and provenance (provider, model, promptVersion, transcriptId). Evidence indexes are resolved server-side into the transcript passages they cite, so each item arrives with `{ segmentIndex, startSeconds, endSeconds, speaker, text }`.

Read-only. Suggestions stay `proposed` and are not action items; promoting them is #65. Nothing here modifies minutes.

`analysisRun` is null until the analysis worker finishes. Watch GET /meetings/{{meetingId}}/workflow/events for the transition rather than polling this.

Owner, organizer, or admin only. Creates the official action item and marks the suggestion accepted, in one transaction.

Exactly-once: a duplicate request returns 200 with alreadyReviewed=true and creates no second task and no second notification. A first acceptance returns 201.

The action item's source ('ai') and source_ref (the analysis run id) are set by the server. `source` is not accepted in the request at all.

The assignee is re-checked against current meeting participants; someone who has left the meeting is rejected with 400.

Owner, organizer, or admin only. Marks the suggestion rejected and records the reviewer and timestamp. Creates no action item.

Rejected suggestions are kept: what was offered and turned down is part of the record.

Owner, organizer, or admin only. Edits a suggestion while it is still `proposed`. An accepted or rejected suggestion returns 409: it is a record of what was decided, not a draft.

Editable: title, description, assigneeId, dueDate, priority. Provenance fields are not editable.

item.name: Participants
item.description: Manage participants on a meeting. All requests target `/meetings/{{meetingId}}/participants`. Only the meeting creator or a participant with `role='organizer'` can add / update / remove participants. The last organizer cannot be demoted or removed.

request.description: Returns `{ participants: [...] }` to the meeting owner, participants, and admins. Each row includes `userId`, `name`, `email`, `role`, `addedBy`, `addedAt`. Also available nested on `GET /meetings/{{meetingId}}`.

Adds one or more users to the meeting. Owner, organizer, or admin only. `userIds` is a 1–50 element array of user UUIDs. `role` is optional (default `attendee`); allowed: `organizer`, `attendee`, `optional`.

Idempotent — re-posting an existing `userId` is a no-op (use PATCH to change role). Returns `201 { participants }` containing the current rows for every requested id.

The test script auto-saves the first returned `userId` to `participantUserId` so the PATCH/DELETE requests below work out of the box.

Update a participant's `role` (owner, organizer, or admin only). Empty body returns 400.

Allowed `role`: `organizer`, `attendee`, `optional`.

Demoting the last organizer returns 400.
Removes the participant from the meeting (owner, organizer, or admin only). Returns 204 on success, 404 if not a participant, 400 if they are the last organizer.

item.name: Files
item.description: Upload, list, download, and delete files attached to a meeting. These materials may include audio, but they are separate from the dedicated Meeting Recording workflow used for minutes generation. Max 50 MB; allowed types: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP, TXT, Markdown, and audio.

request.description: Multipart upload for the owner, participants, and admins. Field name must be `file`. Returns `201 { file }`. Auto-saves `fileId` to collection variable.
Returns `{ files: [...] }` for the meeting. The owner, any participant, or an admin can list.

Returns `{ url, expiresAt }` to the owner, participants, and admins. The presigned URL is valid for 60 seconds — paste it into a browser or use it in a fetch to retrieve the file bytes directly from MinIO.
Hard delete — removes the DB row and the MinIO object. Returns 204. Only the owner, an organizer, or an admin can delete.

item.name: Action items
item.description: Create, list, update, and delete action items attached to a meeting. Any meeting participant (including the creator) can CRUD action items.

item.name: List personal or owned-meeting action items

query.description: mine returns caller-assigned items; owned returns every item in meetings owned by the caller

request.description: Returns `{ actionItems }`. Scope defaults to `mine`; use `owned` for the meeting-owner Overall view, including other assignees and unassigned items.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Write the design doc",
  "description": "Capture decisions from today",
  "assigneeId": "<user-uuid>",
  "dueDate": "2026-05-10T17:00:00+10:00",
  "priority": "high"
}

request.description: Creates an action item (owner, participants, or admin). `title` is required (≤255 chars). `assigneeId`, `dueDate`, `description`, `priority` are optional. Defaults: `status='todo'`, `priority='medium'`, `source='manual'`. Auto-saves `actionItemId` to collection variable.

query.description: Optional: filter to items assigned to a user

request.description: Returns `{ actionItems: [...] }` to the owner, participants, and admins, ordered by `createdAt DESC`. Supports optional `status` and `assigneeId` query filters. Each action item includes derived `isOverdue` and `dueState` fields; overdue is not a persisted status.
Returns `{ actionItem }` with full action item detail, including derived `isOverdue` and `dueState`. The meeting owner, participants, admins, and the assigned user can view it.

Partial update — send only the fields to change. Owner, participants, and admins can change any field; a non-participant assignee can change only `status`. Allowed: `title`, `description`, `assigneeId`, `dueDate`, `status`, `priority`. Empty body returns 400. Transitioning `status` to `completed` stamps `completedAt`; transitioning away clears it.
Hard delete. Returns 204 on success, 404 if not found. Any meeting participant, the owner, or an admin can delete.

Attendee or optional participant only (not the owner). Message is trimmed, 1–2000 characters. Returns 201 { changeRequest: { id, meetingId, userId, message, createdAt } }. Sender identity comes from the token. Repeated submissions create separate messages. Also creates one owner-only meeting_change_requested notification atomically, with entityType meeting, entityId meetingId, meeting title, and sender/message detail. Read through GET /notifications or /notifications/summary.

Only the meeting owner may read these messages; admin and organizer roles do not bypass this restriction. Returns 200 { changeRequests: [...] }, newest first, or [] when none. Errors: 400 invalid UUID, 401 unauthenticated, 403 not owner, 404 meeting or participant missing.

Owner only, with no admin/organizer bypass. Returns 200 { changeRequests: [{ id, meetingId, userId, senderName, message, createdAt }] }, newest first; empty inbox returns []. Errors: 400 invalid meeting UUID, 401 unauthenticated, 403 non-owner, 404 missing meeting. Reading does not mark requests resolved.

Owner only. No body. Returns 200 { changeRequest } with readAt timestamp, preserved on repeated calls. 400 invalid UUIDs; 401 unauthenticated; 403 non-owner; 404 missing meeting/request or request in another meeting. All request responses include readAt (null when unread); lists stay newest first by createdAt regardless of read status. Also marks the matching main notification read.
